correctness.rationale: With θ'=1 and w=r^(-2), the solution w(t)=exp(2κt)(w(0)−2∫₀ᵗexp(−2κs)sin²(θ₀+s)ds) is valid in original time. The bracket strictly decreases on every positive-length interval for a nonzero initial state; its first zero forces r→∞, while positivity gives a smooth solution. This proves the strict inequality for τ>t, including equality as the escape boundary. The weighted rotating vectors span the plane on every interval, giving positive definite nested Gram matrices. Taking the squared modulus of the weighted second harmonic in the determinant yields, for κ>0, exp(−2κt)((sinh(κt)/κ)²−sin²t)/(1+κ²), with neutral determinant t²−sin²t. For κ>0 the infinite-time condition is the non-strict limiting ellipse inequality. On its boundary w is the shifted positive periodic tail integral; differences at a fixed phase grow by exp(4πκ) each revolution. Interior states converge to zero. In the neutral case every nonzero initial direction has divergent squared-sine integral. Subtracting the limiting area therefore gives S, not A, for the long-time asymptotics. Expanding the inverse square root in q=exp(−2κt) gives first coefficient 1+2κ²sin²t and the two extremal subsequences. On compact u>0 intervals the crossover denominator stays away from zero and the oscillatory correction is uniformly O(κ²). At small t the hyperbolic and trigonometric expansions cancel the terms of degree two and give det Q=(t⁴/3)(1−2κt+Oκ(t²)).
residual_risks: The independent four-case time-and-angle quadrature only corroborates the area calculation. The global lifetime and asymptotic conclusions rest on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Original-time survival measured over initial states addresses a quantitative question not answered by classifying point trajectories or the limit cycle. The exact reference law separates complete states from finite-time escape, exhibits a persistent phase modulation rather than a constant exponential prefactor, and specifies the compact-uniform transition from algebraic to exponential tails. These are useful benchmarks for the critical rigid flow even though the required area calculation is elementary.
